result.title: Agent Learning via Early Experience
result.authors: Kai Zhang, Xiangchao Chen, Bo Liu, Tianci Xue, Zeyi Liao, Zhihan Liu, Xiyao Wang, Yuting Ning, Zhaorun Chen, Xiaohan Fu, Jian Xie, Yuxuan Sun, Boyu Gou, Qi Qi, Zihang Meng, Jianwei Yang, Ning Zhang, Xian Li, Ashish Shah, Dat Huynh, Hengduo Li, Zi Yang, Sara Cao, Lawrence Jang, Shuyan Zhou, Jiacheng Zhu, Huan Sun, Jason Weston, Yu Su, Yifan Wu (Meta Superintelligence Labs / FAIR at Meta / The Ohio State University)
result.sections_read: arXiv API record (title/authors/date/comment); full HTML v3: abstract, 1 Introduction, 2 Related Work (2.1, 2.2 incl. World Models and Self-Reflection paragraphs), 3 Preliminaries, 4 Early Experience (4.1 notation, 4.2 Implicit World Modeling with Eq. 3, 4.3 Self-Reflection with Eq. 4), 5 Experiments (5.1 setup, 5.2 Effectiveness Table 1, 5.3 OOD Table 2, 5.4 RL following early experience Fig. 3), 6 Discussion (6.1 human-data amount, 6.2 branching factor, 6.3 baselines Table 3: Long CoT / STaR / DPO, 6.4 model scaling incl. LoRA at 70B), 7 Conclusion, Appendix A contribution statement, Appendix B.2 setup, Appendix C per-environment data-construction details (ALFWorld, WebShop, BFCLv3, Tau-Bench, SearchQA, ScienceWorld, TravelPlanner, WebArena) and Table 4 ALFWorld full results; Appendix B.1 Self-Reflection Prompt Template read verbatim from the PDF (pages 13-16 via the VM) because it renders as an image in the HTML.
result.what_is_learned_and_how: Weights change (full-parameter SFT for 3B/7B/8B; LoRA at 70B), at training time only, with the policy pi_theta and the "world model" sharing the same parameters theta; nothing is updated at test time and there is no external memory store. The signal is reward-free: starting from expert states s_i in D_expert, the initial policy proposes K alternative actions a_i^j (sampled at temperature 1.0, canonicalised, deduplicated, invalid ones replaced by random admissible actions), each is executed in the environment, and the observed next state s_i^j becomes the supervision ("the resulting future states serve as supervision without reward signals"). Implicit world modeling (IWM) trains next-token prediction of s_i^j given (s_i, a_i^j) over D_rollout (up to an order of magnitude larger than D_expert; e.g. 21,031 x 9 = 189,279 triplets on ALFWorld) for one epoch, then continues with ordinary imitation on D_expert inside the same step budget as the IL baseline. Self-reflection (SR) prompts the same model with the state, expert action, expert next state, and each alternative action with its resulting state, and asks for an "internal monologue" c_i^j explaining why the expert action is preferable; the model is then trained on log p(c_i^j, a_i | s_i), i.e. to emit the reflection and then the expert action, with D_refl mixed into D_expert (filtered to drop reflections that end up endorsing a non-expert action). Both are framed as "mid-training" between imitation learning and RL; GRPO can then be run from the resulting checkpoint where verifiable rewards exist.
result.what_it_tells_us_to_parent: The paper externalises one specific thinking move and shows it is worth training into weights: at a decision point, (1) "analyze the situation and the goal", (2) "compare the possible actions, explaining why each may be less optimal", (3) "justify why the expert action is most suitable, grounded in the expected outcome", (4) "highlight any relevant clues, constraints, or consequences from the situation", with the guideline "stay strictly within the provided information" (the B.1 prompt). The key parenting-relevant finding is the grounding requirement: STaR-style rationales written for the correct action without seeing the alternatives' outcomes are "ungrounded" and "potentially contain hallucinated facts", and fine-tuning on them degrades performance (WebShop 47.3 -> 25.0, ALFWorld 80.5 -> 74.2 on Llama-3.1-8B), whereas the same kind of rationale written after observing what the wrong action actually did helps (58.2 / 85.2). So the teachable disposition is: before writing a lesson, obtain the counterfactual outcome (try the alternative, look at the error message or page state), then write a contrastive lesson that names the constraint violated ("it exceeds the $20 budget constraint specified in the query"), a lesson "that generalizes beyond this specific item". Two quantitative habits also transfer: the branching factor (SR works best with a "modest K (e.g., 2-4)" alternatives per state, because "current models have limited capacity to reason over many alternatives and outcomes in a single context", whereas IWM keeps improving with larger K), and the quality filter (discard a reflection whose "concluded action did not match the expert action", i.e. do not store a lesson whose conclusion contradicts the evidence). Finally, the paper treats predicting what will happen next (IWM) as a separate perceptual skill from justifying choices (SR); the former is cheap and scales with breadth of exploration, the latter is reasoning-heavy and pays off most where errors are logical or long-horizon (TravelPlanner +12.8 to +15.0, ScienceWorld +13.3).
competencies_implied: propose alternatives and observe their consequences before judging
write contrastive lessons grounded in observed outcomes, not imagined ones
name the violated constraint so the lesson generalises
predict the next state from state and action (implicit world model)
keep the number of alternatives compared small enough to reason over
discard a reflection whose conclusion contradicts the evidence
stay strictly within the provided information when reflecting
turn own rollouts into supervision without a reward
result.relevance_to_links: Link A (the write): this is the closest published evidence that the write regime the project adopts (child-authored reflection text -> next-token SFT into the same weights) produces behaviour that shows up outside the context where it was written, across eight environments and three model families including Qwen2.5-7B; and the STaR control is exactly the project's provenance/confabulation point: a rationale with no traceable environmental source (the alternative's real outcome) is worse than no rationale (Table 3). Link B (parenting installs the form): the paper does not have a parent; the reflection form is installed by a fixed prompt template applied at data-generation time, and the child is then trained to emit that form unprompted (log p(c, a | s)); this is a hardcoded baseline in Rohin's sense ("write one contrastive monologue per (state, alternative) pair, K = 2-4"), not a learned discretionary judgement of what is worth reflecting on, and there is no test of whether the trained model goes on to reflect well on new experience without the template. Link C (integrated loop improves later learning): section 5.4 is a one-step version of H2: with GRPO recipe, hyperparameters and step count held fixed and only the starting checkpoint varied, early-experience checkpoints reach "higher post-RL ceilings" and on ALFWorld "the performance gap grows during RL training" (IL+RL 93.8 vs SR+RL 98.5 vs IWM+RL 97.7 on Llama-3.1-8B; RL from the raw instruct model is worst and unstable), which is a slope-and-ceiling claim about later learning, though measured on the same task rather than an unseen gym and with a single consolidation stage rather than a running loop. Differences from the dream-state design: full-parameter SFT (LoRA only at 70B, and there as a compute shortcut, not a frozen-base commitment); one offline mid-training pass rather than repeated sleep from a growing corpus; supervision anchored to expert demonstrations at every state (D_expert is required as the branching point and as the target action, so the child never has to decide what the right action was - it only explains a given one); the environment, not a parent or person, is the only external source; and there is no memory adapter or canonical-frame retrieval, so the paper speaks to behaviour (rank-8-type) consolidation and says nothing about fact memory. It is therefore a strong citation for "the regime works and grounding is what separates useful from harmful self-generated data", and a clear foil for what parenting adds: the discretionary, unprompted version of the same move, sustained over many sleeps, without an expert action to lean on.
result.evidence_scale: Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B (plus Llama-3.3-70B with LoRA on WebArena) on eight environments (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, TravelPlanner, BFCLv3, Tau-Bench Retail, SearchQA, WebShop, WebArena-Lite); IWM and SR beat imitation learning in every cell of Table 1 (e.g. Qwen-2.5-7B WebShop 51.6 -> 56.2 IWM / 62.2 SR; TravelPlanner 16.7 -> 22.2 / 31.7; ALFWorld 78.1 -> 82.8 / 82.0), with OOD gains of similar size and 1/8 of demonstrations plus early experience beating full-data IL on WebShop. Controls: identical optimisation step budget and prompt format as the IL baseline; Long-CoT, STaR-style ungrounded rationales and DPO on the same rollouts as baselines (STaR and Long-CoT degrade IL, DPO collapses within tens of steps); GRPO with identical hyperparameters and steps varied only by starting checkpoint; branching-factor and demonstration-budget ablations on Llama-3.1-8B.

result.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning
result.authors: Idan Shenfeld, Mehul Damani, Jonas Hübotter, Pulkit Agrawal (MIT Improbable AI Lab; Hübotter at ETH Zurich)
result.venue_or_status: arXiv preprint (v2, cs.LG); no venue listed on the abs page that I could retrieve. Code/datasets at idanshenfeld.com/SDFT. Concurrent sibling papers it names: Zhao et al. 2601.18734 (Self-Distilled Reasoner) and Hübotter et al. 2601.20802 (RL via self-distillation).
result.sections_read: Abstract; Sec 1 Intro; Sec 2 Related Work; Sec 3 method incl. 3.1 (IRL derivation) and 3.2 (validating the ICL assumption); Sec 4.1-4.6 experiments; Sec 5 Discussion and Limitations; Appendix A.1 (KL estimators), A.2 (teacher context ablation), A.3 (teacher choice: frozen base vs student vs EMA); Appendix B.1-B.3 (training, eval, datasets); Algorithm 1; Tables 1-5. Read via arxiv.org/html/2601.19897v2.
result.what_is_learned_and_how: Weights change: full fine-tuning of all parameters of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (no LoRA, no memory store, no prompt change at test time). The signal is the model's own demonstration-conditioned distribution: for each prompt x with an external demonstration c, the student pi_theta(.|x) samples ONE on-policy rollout y, and the teacher -- the same model (an EMA copy of the student, alpha 0.01-0.05) conditioned on the template "<Question> This is an example for a response to the question: <Demonstration> Now answer with a response of your own, including the thinking process:" -- scores the same tokens; the loss is a per-token analytic KL between student and teacher logits over the vocabulary (reverse KL in theory, forward KL best in practice), with the first few tokens masked so the student does not inherit "Based on the text..." artifacts. Sec 3.1 shows this equals on-policy RL against an implicit reward r_t = log pi(y_t|y<t,x,c) - log pi_k(y_t|y<t,x) under an "In-Context Assumption" (the demo-conditioned model approximates the trust-region-optimal next policy). All of this happens at training time with the demonstration available; at test time the student answers with no demonstration and no context. For knowledge acquisition the "demonstration" is the article text plus a worked QA answer (text+answer 89% strict vs text-only 75%, A.2). Cost ~2.5x FLOPs and ~4x wall-clock vs SFT.
result.what_it_tells_us_to_parent: The behaviour SDFT externalises is: take an external correction/demonstration and re-express it "with a response of your own, including the thinking process" -- the authors verify on 50 ToolAlpaca traces that the teacher is "reconstructing a correct reasoning process rather than merely copying the expert output", and they measure that this self-restated target stays near the base distribution (0.68 nats KL to base vs 1.26 for SFT-on-the-demonstration), which they call the "Minimal Deviation" condition and credit for the absence of forgetting. So a parent could teach the child: (1) never store the parent's words or the environment's output verbatim -- restate it in first person with your own reasoning, anchored to how you already talk; (2) when perceiving a source, pair the raw text with a worked/resolved instance (source + answer beats source alone, A.2), i.e. perceive a fact through a use of it; (3) let the training target be your own attempt, corrected by your demonstration-aware self, not the parent's text (offline distillation from the very same teacher underperforms the on-policy version, Fig 6 -- "the benefits cannot be attributed solely to teacher quality"); (4) strip context-referencing scaffolding ("Following the example...") from what gets written, otherwise the child carries markers of a context it no longer has (their "Learned Artifacts" failure mode -- the analogue of our leakage/provenance gate); (5) keep your own thinking style while absorbing answer-only supervision (Olmo-3-7B-Think: SDFT 43.7% with 4180 tokens vs SFT 23.5% with 3273 tokens -- reasoning depth preserved). The paper hardcodes all of this in a template and a loss; nothing about when or how much to write is learned, and it explicitly reports it "struggles when the desired behavior requires a fundamental shift in the model's generation patterns" (failed to turn a non-reasoning model into a CoT model) -- which is exactly the kind of change parenting is supposed to make.
competencies_implied: restate an external demonstration in own words with own reasoning
perceive a source through a worked instance (text + answer)
train on own attempt corrected by demo-aware self, not on the demonstration
stay close to own prior distribution while absorbing new content (minimal deviation)
strip context-referencing artifacts before the write
preserve own reasoning depth under answer-only supervision
accumulate skills sequentially without regression
result.evidence_scale: Mostly Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, full fine-tuning on one H200, 3 seeds with 95% CI, per-baseline hyperparameter sweeps; a 3B/7B/14B scaling sweep on Science QA (3B underperforms SFT; 7B +4 pts; 14B +7 pts over SFT) and Olmo-3-7B-Think for answer-only supervision. Skill tasks (Table 5): SciKnowEval chemistry 70.2 vs SFT 66.2 with prior-capability average 64.5 vs 53.4 (base 65.5); ToolAlpaca 70.6 vs 63.2, prior 65.4 vs 56.0; HuatuoGPT-o1 medical 40.2 vs 35.5, prior 65.4 vs 60.2; knowledge acquisition on ~200K tokens of 2025-disaster Wikipedia: strict 89 vs SFT 80 vs CPT 9 (oracle RAG 91), OOD "indirect" questions 98 vs 80; sequential 3-skill run retains each skill (Fig 3) where SFT oscillates. Controls: SFT, DFT, SFT+re-invoke, CPT, oracle RAG, offline SFT/distillation from the identical teacher (Fig 6), frozen-base vs student vs EMA teacher (A.3), pass@k to 128 to rule out entropy collapse, KL-to-base of teacher vs SFT model.
result.relevance_to_links: Link A (the write): strong supporting evidence for the mechanism we adopt but did not invent. It shows that a model's own restatement of an external input, in its own voice with its own reasoning, is far better post-training data than the raw input -- CPT on the source text 9% strict, SFT on QA pairs 80%, self-restated on-policy target 89% and 98% on indirect/OOD questions, i.e. the fact is 'incorporated into the model's broader knowledge base' rather than memorised narrowly. This is the same direction as SEQ-049 (child-authored frames beat synthetic ones) and fits the 'not self-distillation' provenance defence: despite the name, every SDFT target traces to an external c (demonstration or article+answer); the model contributes compression and register conversion, not information. It also gives a measurable for 'perceived well enough to be written': KL of the restatement to the base distribution (theirs 0.68 vs 1.26 nats) -- a candidate metric for our corpus. Link B (parenting installs the form): SDFT does NOT learn the form; the template prompt and KL loss are the hardcoded '16 things per event' baseline, not discretionary memory. Nothing here about deciding importance, how much to think, or what to keep. Worse for us, its stated limitation -- cannot induce 'a fundamental shift in the model's generation patterns' (non-reasoning to CoT failed) -- says a self-teacher alone will not install a new thinking form; that is precisely where the parent corpus must do work SDFT cannot. Link C (integrated loop improves later learning): only partial. The sequential 3-skill run shows accumulation without regression (a level result), but there is no measurement that earlier learning makes later learning faster -- no slope, no 2x2, no H2 analogue. Differences from our frozen-base + one LoRA rewritten at sleep: (i) full fine-tuning of all 7B parameters, and A.3 found a FROZEN-base teacher 'consistently underperforms' because it does not track progress -- their EMA teacher is a slowly moving copy of the whole model, whereas our frozen base + fresh LoRA is closer to their worst-performing teacher configuration unless the LoRA is stacked into the teacher; (ii) the write is a logit-level KL on a live rollout at the moment the demonstration is present, not SFT at sleep on accumulated thought text -- SDFT needs the demonstration in context during training, so it is a wake-time on-policy compile, not a sleep-time replay; (iii) one rollout per prompt, no repetition or canonical-frame scaffolding, 2.5x FLOPs; (iv) student sees a bare question, not a completion-retrieval frame. A convertible idea for our compile step: use the child's own episode+parent-correction-conditioned distribution as the teacher for the bare-frame student, with first-token masking as the leakage gate.
